original_value: AbstractMotivationComputational biologists face many challenges related to data size, and they need to manage complicated analyses often including multiple stages and multiple tools, all of which must be deployed to modern infrastructures. To address these challenges and maintain reproducibility of results, researchers need (i) a reliable way to run processing stages in any computational environment, (ii) a well-defined way to orchestrate those processing stages and (iii) a data management layer that tracks data as it moves through the processing pipeline.ResultsPachyderm is an open-source workflow system and data management framework that fulfils these needs by creating a data pipelining and data versioning layer on top of projects from the container ecosystem, having Kubernetes as the backbone for container orchestration. We adapted Pachyderm and demonstrated its attractive properties in bioinformatics. A Helm Chart was created so that researchers can use Pachyderm in multiple scenarios. The Pachyderm File System was extended to support block storage. A wrapper for initiating Pachyderm on cloud-agnostic virtual infrastructures was created. The benefits of Pachyderm are illustrated via a large metabolomics workflow, demonstrating that Pachyderm enables efficient and sustainable data science workflows while maintaining reproducibility and scalability.Availability and implementationPachyderm is available from https://github.com/pachyderm/pachyderm. The Pachyderm Helm Chart is available from https://github.com/kubernetes/charts/tree/master/stable/pachyderm. Pachyderm is available out-of-the-box from the PhenoMeNal VRE (https://github.com/phnmnl/KubeNow-plugin) and general Kubernetes environments instantiated via KubeNow. The code of the workflow used for the analysis is available on GitHub (https://github.com/pharmbio/LC-MS-Pachyderm).Supplementary informationSupplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

result.paraphrase: Abstract and motivation: Computational biologists must cope with large data volumes and complex analyses that often span multiple stages and tools, all of which need deployment on modern infrastructure. To meet these challenges and ensure reproducible results, researchers require: (i) a dependable way to execute processing stages in any computational environment, (ii) a clearly defined method for coordinating those stages, and (iii) a data management layer that follows data as it travels through the pipeline. Results: Pachyderm is an open-source workflow system and data management framework that addresses these needs by adding data pipelining and data versioning on top of container-ecosystem projects, with Kubernetes serving as the orchestration backbone. We adapted Pachyderm and demonstrated its appealing features in bioinformatics. A Helm Chart was produced to let researchers use Pachyderm in a range of scenarios. The Pachyderm File System was expanded to support block storage. A wrapper for launching Pachyderm on cloud-agnostic virtual infrastructures was also created. Its benefits are shown through a large metabolomics workflow, illustrating that Pachyderm supports efficient, sustainable data science workflows while preserving reproducibility and scalability. Availability and implementation: Pachyderm is available at https://github.com/pachyderm/pachyderm. The Pachyderm Helm Chart is available at https://github.com/kubernetes/charts/tree/master/stable/pachyderm. Out-of-the-box access to Pachyderm is provided by the PhenoMeNal VRE (https://github.com/phnmnl/KubeNow-plugin) and by general Kubernetes environments instantiated through KubeNow. The workflow code used for the analysis is available on GitHub (https://github.com/pharmbio/LC-MS-Pachyderm). Supplementary information: Supplementary data are available online at Bioinformatics.
